teaser.text: China Mobile Limited sells far more than phone calls: it connects people, homes and organisations, then adds the computing, content and technical services that run through those connections. To understand its business, follow what it sells, who pays, and how a customer’s yuan becomes revenue, cost and cash.

stock.title: China Mobile stock forecast
stock.meta_description: China Mobile's weighted forecast is near today's share price, with dividends doing much of the work while cash conversion remains the key test.
stock.opening: The probability-weighted forecast points to HKD79.44 in October 2027 and HKD79.18 in October 2029. It hinges on cash conversion from computing investment and the durability of the dividend.
stock.closing: The full memo explains China Mobile’s business, rivals, management choices and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could China Mobile’s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to a nearly flat share price but a positive total return, because dividends do much of the work. The probability-weighted price is HKD79.44 in October 2027, HKD79.20 in October 2028 and HKD79.18 in October 2029, versus HKD79.95 today. Including dividends, those returns are 6%, 13% and 20%.
The three-year range is wide: HKD49.79 in the bear case to HKD109.09 in the bull case. The base case has the highest probability at 55%, against 25% for the bear case and 20% for the bull case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for China Mobile?

paragraphs.text: The base multiple stays at 3.5x. That fits a mature telecom operator whose recurring scale and net cash support the valuation, but whose falling mobile monetization limits a major re-rating. The bear case combines weaker EBITDA with a falling multiple; the bull case combines better operating performance with a higher multiple.

EBITDA is the main operating driver. The base case starts with 2025 EBITDA of CNY338,931 million and holds it broadly flat in 2027. It then grows 1.5% annually to CNY344,015 million and CNY349,175 million. The restraint reflects falling communications income, while computing-services revenue grew 14.0% in the first half of 2026 and intelligent-computing utilization exceeded 90%. The bear case applies a 3% annual decline, ending at CNY309,332 million; the bull case starts with 2% growth and then uses 4% annual growth, reaching CNY373,920 million.

blocks.heading: How much cash does China Mobile really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow means cash remaining after investment, but the definition matters. Deducting capital spending, lease payments and interest from 2025 operating cash flow leaves RMB41,421 million. China Mobile’s own measure was RMB82,041 million because it uses a different investment definition and does not separately deduct those payments.

dividend.opening: China Mobile pays HK$5.27 per share, up from HK$5.09. In 2025, strict free cash flow was RMB41,421 million against RMB103,410 million of dividends paid, so the year's cash did not cover the dividend.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines China Mobile's business, its rivals, its management and the risks around its strategy.

blocks.heading: How much does China Mobile pay per share over the years shown?

paragraphs.text: China Mobile paid RMB103,410 million in dividends in 2025. The annual declared dividend rose to HK$5.27 per share from HK$5.09, despite falling EPS. The cash dividend was about 2.5 times strict free cash flow and exceeded the company’s own measure. The difference does not prove an immediate funding crisis, but it shows that the year’s distribution relied on existing financial assets or other funding.

blocks.heading: What could change China Mobile's dividend?

paragraphs.text: Management plans 2026 capex of RMB136,600 million and a 75.0% dividend payout ratio. That payout is a share of profit, not a guaranteed dividend per share. The plan adds 10 million mobile customers and 18 million integrated broadband customers. It also targets more than 48,000 PFLOPS, a measure of computing speed, of added intelligent-computing capacity.

Dividends grow gradually in the base case from CNY4.7 per share to CNY5.0. The path follows the 75% payout target and a near-term EPS estimate close to 2025 diluted EPS of CNY6.30. The bear case falls from CNY4.3 to CNY3.8 because weak earnings and cash conversion reduce payout capacity. The bull case rises from CNY4.8 to CNY5.6 if computing growth converts into earnings and cash.

During 2028–2029, persistent cash generation below dividends and investment needs would weaken confidence in both the dividend and the multiple. The 2025 cash-flow shortfall shows why this test matters.

blocks.heading: What is China Mobile's dividend yield today against its price?

paragraphs.text: Bear and base cases carry probabilities of 25% and 55%. The bull case carries 20%. At HK$79.95, the 10.9x forward P/E frames the stock as an income investment. Its 6.6% dividend yield makes cash conversion decisive.

blocks.heading: What has China Mobile guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: Management set 2026 capital expenditure at RMB136,600 million, a year-on-year decrease of 9.5%. Capital expenditure pays for assets that serve customers for years, such as radio equipment, fibre, servers and data centres. The budget is one pool, however. China Mobile can reduce spending on mature networks while adding servers and AI facilities. It is like a city building fewer roads while expanding warehouses: total construction falls, but one kind of capacity grows.

Computing networks received RMB15.6 billion in the plan, while conventional communications-network spending declined. Management also targets 10 million additional mobile customers and 18 million additional integrated broadband customers. It wants more than 48,000 PFLOPS of additional intelligent-computing capacity, a measure of processing speed for demanding workloads.

blocks.heading: Has China Mobile kept its dividend promise?

paragraphs.text: China Mobile has delivered clearer evidence of alignment through dividends than through the public design of senior executive pay.

Dividends provide a more visible promise. China Mobile reported a payout ratio of 75% for 2025 and a full-year dividend of HK$5.27 per share. A payout ratio measures the share of profit distributed to shareholders.

blocks.heading: What do China Mobile's last eight reported periods show?

paragraphs.text: June-quarter revenue was RMB271,557 million, down 3.0% from a year earlier. Operating income fell 14.7% to RMB49,282 million, and attributable profit declined 7.5% to RMB49,592 million. Operating margin fell from about 20.6% to 18.1%, showing how a network’s costs do not fall automatically when revenue does.
